configuration: The single upstream case of unittest/orthant-cone.cpp on the non-negative orthant of dimension ten. Upstream runs two loops of 1e6 fresh draws, the second repeating the first with one further assertion; both assertions run here on the same 64 frozen draws from ic/<ic>/operands.json, in one loop, with every original assertion active.
observable: the projection onto the non-negative orthant and its residual
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that the swept draws are 64 frozen vectors rather than two loops of 1e6 fresh ones, which is why this check runs in milliseconds where the upstream test takes about two thirds of a second
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on every nonzero number of ic/nominal/operands.json. Perturbing every number rather than a chosen few is deliberate and was measured on earlier leaves of this codebase: a relative change of 2.2e-16 in one component of a rotation or of a frozen vector rounds away in the last bit of an output built from all of them, and moving one component per item left dozens of observables with a spread of exactly zero. Every number still moves by exactly two units in the last place, so this remains the generic numerical-noise calibration and not a physics experiment. A number that is exactly zero is never perturbed, because two ulps above zero is a subnormal, which is a meaningless perturbation of a physical quantity and a parser hazard besides. The worst measured spread is 2.2204e-16 absolute. Every one of the 2 observables moves under the perturbation.
altbuild: none: the same official.cpp compiled at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off against the same pinned source reproduces the -O2 -DNDEBUG result bit-identically for every graded value of this check, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. Eigen fixes the evaluation order of these expressions and the arithmetic is scalar, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate. Repeated on the worker on 2026-09-14 (x86_64, inside the env image): bit-identical.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned source, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead. Repeated on the worker on 2026-09-14 (x86_64, inside the env image): bit-identical.

warrant: The graded quantities are the projection of a ten-vector onto the non-negative orthant and the residual of that projection. Row k is the k-th frozen draw and the column is the coordinate, both fixed by the input file. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 9.99e-01, it admits 1.01e-09. It is physical because the orthant projection is the componentwise positive part, and every fault it can express is of order one: projecting onto the wrong orthant, keeping the negative part, or returning the input unchanged each move a value by between 1e-3 and 1e+0, and a relative error of one part in a thousand injected into the largest graded value lands 989,446 times over the bound. The smallest distance from any frozen draw to the branch boundary at zero is 4.1288e-04, thirteen decades above the two-ulp perturbation, so no draw can change branch under the variant. It is achievable because the positive part is a comparison and a copy, exact in binary64. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst of the 1,280 graded values by 2.2204e-16, using 2.209e-07 of the bound, that is 4,526,137 times of headroom, and the alternative build measured exactly zero.
